questions.title: Read Counts off a Two-Way Table and Apply the Addition Rule - pull the joint and marginal counts from a 2x2 and combine them without double-counting the overlap
Both Conditional Directions from One Table - compute P(A given B) and P(B given A) off the same 2x2 and see that they are different numbers
Why the Two Conditional Directions Differ - work from the joint probability to both conditionals and identify which total each one divides by
Medical Test Bayes Chain - P(disease and positive), then P(positive), then P(disease given positive) from a prevalence, a sensitivity and a false-positive rate
Recover the Joint from the Union, then Condition - solve the addition rule backwards for P(A and B) and use it as the numerator of a conditional
Pre-FRQ Grade a Conditional Reading - a two-way table scenario with a grading checklist, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
